messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "hey folks, quick bench update on the little temperature display. i soldered the header pins onto the sensor board last night, and mounted the screen on a scrap piece of acrylic. the screen is 0.96 inch, 128 by 64, and the sensor is a bme280 i had in the parts drawer. i powered it from the usb port on my laptop, not the bench supply, so the wiring is still pretty simple.

the first reading came up about 1.8 degrees c higher than the room thermometer, but both were sitting in different spots on the desk. i'll leave them side by side for a while before i change anything. the display refreshes every two seconds right now, which is probably more often than it needs to.

i haven't put the board in an enclosure yet. the acrylic is just a temporary mount, and one corner is a little rough from the handsaw. i have a small project box here, but it may be too shallow once the usb cable is plugged in. does anyone know if these boxes usually have enough room for a right-angle cable? i can measure the clearance after work and post it here. no photos yet; i forgot to bring the phone stand to the bench.", "output": "Hey folks, quick bench update on the little temperature display. I soldered the header pins onto the sensor board last night and mounted the screen on a scrap piece of acrylic. The screen is 0.96 inch, 128 by 64, and the sensor is a BME280 I had in the parts drawer. I powered it from the USB port on my laptop, not the bench supply, so the wiring is still pretty simple.

The first reading came up about 1.8 degrees C higher than the room thermometer, but both were sitting in different spots on the desk. I'll leave them side by side for a while before I change anything. The display refreshes every two seconds right now, which is probably more often than it needs to.

I haven't put the board in an enclosure yet. The acrylic is just a temporary mount, and one corner is a little rough from the handsaw. I have a small project box here, but it may be too shallow once the USB cable is plugged in. Does anyone know if these boxes usually have enough room for a right-angle cable? I can measure the clearance after work and post it here. Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "lena: hey all, starting a thread for the May trip so we stop losing details in texts. We’re looking at May 22–27, driving from Portland to Vancouver and then over to Victoria. It’s six of us: Ravi and me, Noah (9), Mira (5), my mom Diane, and Priya. Nothing is booked yet except our aquarium tickets for Saturday.

ravi: I checked the calendar again, and Friday the 22nd is the first day we can all leave. I can take the Subaru, but with six people and bags it’ll be tight. The kids can share the back seat, and Diane says she’s fine in the passenger seat, but we still need to decide what to do with the luggage.

priya: I can bring my small duffel and a backpack, no hard suitcase. I’d rather not rent a second car unless we really need one. If we drive all the way, can we leave Portland by 7:00 a.m.? That should get us to the border before the afternoon traffic, though I’m not sure how much time to add for the crossing.

diane: I’m happy to leave early, but I don’t want to be rushed through breakfast. Could we pack sandwiches the night before and stop somewhere after we cross? I’d also like one proper stretch break for my knee. It’s okay on long drives as long as I get out and walk every couple of hours.

lena: For Vancouver, I found a hotel near Coal Harbour that has two queen beds and a pullout sofa. It’s $318 Canadian a night before tax, and parking is another $42 a night. The room says it sleeps six, but I haven’t called to check whether they count Mira as a full guest. Free cancellation ends May 8.

ravi: That’s more than I expected, but it’s walking distance to the aquarium and the seawall. The cheaper place by the airport is $229 a night, although we’d have to drive in and pay for parking downtown. I can call both hotels at lunch and ask about the bed setup, breakfast, and whether the parking price includes in-and-out privileges.

noah: is the aquarium really booked for 10:30 saturday? i want to see the penguins first and the jellyfish room. also can we get lunch there or should we bring snacks because i get hungry before noon

lena: Yes, the tickets are for 10:30 a.m. on Saturday, May 23. We can stay as long as we like, and I think there’s a café, but I haven’t checked the menu or prices. We should bring a couple of snacks in case the line is long. We’re not adding Science World this time; that would be too much for one day.

priya: On Sunday we could take the 11:00 ferry from Tsawwassen to Swartz Bay, then drive to Victoria. The sailing is about an hour and 35 minutes, but we’d need to arrive early with the car. I saw a fare estimate of $112 for the vehicle and two adults, plus $18 for each extra adult. Kids are less, but I didn’t get the exact amount.

ravi: Can you send the page you used? I saw a different total when I looked, and I’m not sure if it included the reservation fee. I’d rather book a specific sailing than risk lining up, especially with the kids and the bags. We need to leave enough time to check out of the hotel and get to Tsawwassen too.

lena: Here’s what I have so far for the middle of the trip:
1. Friday, May 22: drive Portland to Vancouver; check in and have an easy dinner.
2. Saturday, May 23: aquarium at 10:30; keep the afternoon open for the seawall or a rest.
3. Sunday, May 24: check out, ferry to Victoria, and pick up groceries on the way to the hotel.

priya: I like keeping Sunday light. The hotel in Victoria is a guesthouse near Cook Street Village, $274 Canadian a night for a family suite. It has a small kitchenette and breakfast is not included. They have one parking space per room, but the listing says we have to confirm the Subaru’s height because the garage clearance is low.

diane: The kitchenette would help, and I can make oatmeal for the kids if there’s a pot and bowls. I don’t need a fancy breakfast. Can you ask if the suite is on the ground floor? Stairs are manageable, but I’d rather not carry my suitcase up two flights if there’s another option.

ravi: I messaged the guesthouse this morning. They said the suite is on the second floor, but there’s an elevator. They haven’t confirmed the garage height yet; they asked for the vehicle model, so I sent Subaru Outback, 2021. They said they’ll reply by tomorrow. Cancellation is free until May 12.

lena: For Monday, May 25, the kids want the Royal BC Museum and the harbour. The museum is open until 5, but I can’t tell if we’ll need timed tickets. We could go in the morning, have lunch nearby, and leave the afternoon for Beacon Hill Park if the weather’s decent. No need to cram in Butchart Gardens too.

noah: can we go to the park with the goats? my friend said there are goats at beacon hill and i want to see them. also i want to bring my soccer ball but it might be too big for the car

priya: Beacon Hill has a petting zoo, but their site says it opens seasonally, so we should check the hours for that week. I can bring a small ball instead of the full-size one. For the museum, I didn’t see timed entry on the ticket page, but I only looked quickly. Maybe someone can verify before we buy anything.

diane: Tuesday the 26th could be a slower day. I’d like to walk around the Inner Harbour in the morning and sit somewhere for coffee. If everyone wants to see another garden or shop, I can take a break at the hotel and meet up later. I don’t want the schedule to assume I’m doing every activity.

ravi: Agreed. We should also work out the return route for Wednesday, May 27. The ferry from Victoria back to Tsawwassen is about 1 hour and 35 minutes, then it’s a long drive to Portland. There’s a Coho ferry to Port Angeles, but that adds a border crossing and a different route. I haven’t compared the prices or departure times yet.

lena: I’m leaning toward returning through Tsawwassen because it’s the route we already know, but I’m open to the Coho if it saves a meaningful amount of driving. We should plan a real meal and a break on the way home, not just hope the kids sleep. I can take the first driving shift if we leave early.

priya: I can handle the food list and bring a cooler, but we should agree on how many hotel nights we’re paying for. I counted two in Vancouver and three in Victoria, so five nights total. If we decide to add a night in Vancouver, that changes the ferry day and the hotel price. I don’t think we’ve agreed to that.

diane: Five nights works for me. Please don’t book a room with only one bathroom without checking first; that’s important with six people getting ready in the morning. I can share with Priya if the suite has two separate sleeping areas, but I’d like to know the actual layout before we pay a deposit.

ravi: I’ll put the booking details in one place once we hear from the hotels. For now, we have the aquarium tickets, but no hotel, ferry, museum, or garden tickets. The main open things seem to be the car space, exact room setup, and the return ferry. Tell me if I missed something.

lena: Specific question for everyone: should I try to reserve the larger Vancouver hotel and the Tsawwassen ferry first, or wait until we confirm the Victoria suite’s garage clearance and room layout? We have $1,600 set aside for lodging and ferries before food, and I don’t want to spend it in the wrong order. maya: on the q&a, we did run out of time faster than i expected. the speaker stayed for a few minutes after, but i know not everyone could hang around. would setting aside the last 10 minutes just for questions make it feel less rushed? also your idea about putting the book list in the event email is a good one; i can ask the desk staff to add it next time.
maya: for context, we had about 55 chairs set up, and the event started at 6:30. i don't want to assume the issue was only volume; the side door was opening during the first part, too. if that was distracting, you can mention that as well.

Keep casual tone, contractions, emoji, and the original request. Return correct text unchanged.", "input": "Mara: Thanks for the detailed ride notes, Jules. Your point about the front truck feeling twitchy on the cracked path is useful. We’d been testing on smooth pavement, so we weren’t seeing that same movement. I’m pulling the setup notes into this thread so we can compare the changes clearly.

Jules: Yep, the rough section by the old rail bridge is where I noticed it most. At about 18 mph, the board wandered when I crossed the seams. It wasn’t a speed wobble, exactly; it just took more small corrections than my other setup. The rear felt planted the whole time.

Mara: Got it. You also mentioned that the board was easier to pump after you changed the front bushings. Which ones did you swap in? I have the stock 90a barrels listed on your original build sheet, but I don’t want to assume those were still on the board during the ride.

Jules: I put in the 87a roadside bushings from the spare kit, with the stock roadside washers. The boardside barrels are still 90a. I tightened the kingpin nut about a quarter turn after the first run, then backed it off a little when the return felt slow.

Devin: That’s a helpful detail. The truck has a 50-degree baseplate, and a softer roadside bushing can make the steering feel more responsive without changing the baseplate angle. A quarter turn can also be a noticeable adjustment on that setup. Did you keep the same wheel wells and risers as before?

Jules: Yes, same 1/8-inch risers and the 70 mm wheels. I didn’t get any wheel bite, even when I leaned hard through the parking-lot turns. The wheels are the 78a ones, not the 80a set from the photos. I should’ve called that out earlier.

Mara: No worries, that’s exactly the kind of context we need. I’ll update the ride log to show the 78a wheels and the bushing change. Your other comment was that the deck felt comfortable underfoot but flexed more than you expected near the rear bolts. Did you notice that loaded or just while carrying it?

Jules: Loaded, with my backpack on. I’m around 82 kg, and the pack was maybe 6 kg. I felt a little extra give when I shifted back to push, but there wasn’t a creak or any visible separation around the inserts. The deck is the 38-inch maple one with the shallow rocker.

Inez: Thanks, Jules. That’s a useful distinction. The 38-inch deck has a longer wheelbase than the sample we used for the product photos, and that can change how flex feels even when the layup is the same. Could you share which mounting holes you used? The inner pair changes the wheelbase by about half an inch.

Jules: I used the outer holes, for the longer wheelbase. I prefer the extra room for my stance, especially on the bike path. My front foot sits just behind the front bolts, and my back foot is a few inches ahead of the tail. I didn’t measure the exact distance.

Mara: That matches the build sheet. I’m replying to your overall feedback here: we can describe the deck as having noticeable flex under a loaded stance, but I wouldn’t call that a defect based on one ride. We should keep the wording specific to what you felt and avoid implying that you tested it with a heavier load.

Jules: That works for me. I wasn’t trying to say it’s unsafe or that the deck is damaged. It felt comfortable, and the flex didn’t bother me while cruising. I just expected it to feel stiffer because the product page calls the maple layup “firm and supportive.”

Devin: Fair point about that wording. “Firm and supportive” doesn’t give much context for rider weight or wheelbase. We could add a note that perceived flex varies with stance, load, and mounting position. I’d keep your quote as feedback, though, since it explains what led to the expectation.

Mara: Agreed. I’ll include the quote in the internal notes and suggest a more specific line for the page, not replace the current copy yet. There’s also your note about the grip tape collecting grit near the tail. Was that after the wet ride on Saturday, or did it happen during the dry test?

Jules: Dry test. I brushed the deck off before I started, but little bits of gravel stuck to the tape after the path. They came off with a stiff nylon brush. The tape still felt grippy under my shoes, and the edges weren’t lifting. I haven’t ridden it in rain.

Inez: Good to know. The tape is the coarse black sheet from the current batch, and we haven’t changed the grit size on that run. I’ll note that it held small gravel but cleaned up with a brush. Since you haven’t ridden in rain, let’s leave wet-weather grip out of the summary.

Owen: I checked the hardware list against Mara’s notes: stainless 1.5-inch bolts, 1/8-inch risers, and the standard 50-degree trucks. Nothing in the spec sheet conflicts with Jules’s setup. The photos show the 80a wheels, so we should label them as studio photos rather than use them to identify the ride configuration.

Mara: 1. Ride notes to carry forward: 78a, 70 mm wheels; 87a roadside bushings with 90a boardside barrels; stock roadside washers; outer mounting holes; and no reported wheel bite. 2. Deck feedback: comfortable, with noticeable flex under a backpack load. 3. Grip feedback: gravel collected on a dry path and brushed off; no rain test.

Rae: Thanks, Jules, for taking the time to write this up and for being precise about what you did and didn’t test. We’ll use the setup details when we review the product-page wording. If you get another chance to ride the board, the same route with the original bushings would make a useful comparison, but there’s no pressure to do another test.", "output": "Mara: Thanks for the detailed ride notes, Jules.
